title: The 1947 New Orleans film photo and turning down Armstrong's band again
summary: Looking at a photo in Jazz People, he recalls the bandmates and asking $450 a week, which Armstrong's road manager refused.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: We were opening the book Jazz People a while ago to that photograph of you with Louis Armstrong...
Right. And you were reminded of something. Right?
Yes, I was reminded...what was I reminded of...? There's Barney Bigard who's gone, Pops, Bud Scott, Kid Ory, Zutty Singleton. Charlie Beal suffered a stroke
recently, but he's recovered about 85 percent. And being the kid, I'm still here.
You really look like a kid there.
I was a kid. I was somewhere in my early twenties.
What you said was that after that session they asked you to join Louis' band.

1947. Joe Glaser's office had called me, and he took the picture for me. So after the show, after the picture, they decided that Louis should front a Dixieland band or a small band. And naturally, after working in the band, I was offered the job. I asked for $450 a week, and Frenchy, who was the road manager, and I guess Joe Glaser's sidekick, too, said, 'What!? For a bass player?' And I said, 'Yes, for a bass player. What's $450? You guys make $25,000 a night when the band plays.' So he said, 'That's too much for a bass player.' So I said, 'Okay, forget it.'
